design_name: INFEASIBLE AS STATED - feasible substitute: Rete-mirabile-inspired finned evaporator surface for a heat pump (COP > 3 with external ambient heat source)
inspiration_source: Counter-current rete mirabile (tuna, penguin feet) and branched, high-area fin geometry of elephant ears / bird air sacs; the request itself has no physically valid biological or technical analog
physical_mechanism: IMPORTANT FEASIBILITY NOTE: The request as stated is physically impossible. In a completely closed, adiabatic system without any energy input, the first law of thermodynamics (dU = dQ - dW with dQ = 0 across the boundary and no work input) forbids any sustained net heat output; a surface that permanently releases more heat than it receives is a perpetual motion machine of the first kind. No biomimetic structure, microstructure or material can circumvent this, and no cross-domain analog exists. A 'Wirkungsgrad' above 300 % is only meaningful as a coefficient of performance (COP) of a heat pump, which is an OPEN system: it pumps heat Q_amb from an external low-temperature reservoir (air, ground, water) using work W, delivering Q_h = Q_amb + W, so Q_h/W > 3 is possible while energy is conserved (Carnot limit COP_max = T_h/(T_h - T_c), e.g. 308 K/25 K ~ 12). The concept proposed here is therefore a legitimate substitute, NOT a solution to the stated request: a bio-inspired, high-area, counter-current finned evaporator surface that improves heat uptake from the ambient source and thus raises a heat pump's real COP. The modeled physics is steady 1D fin conduction with convective exchange, d2T/dx2 - (h*P/(k*A_c))*(T - T_amb) = 0, which strictly conserves energy. Any result from this model must not be presented as heat generation from nothing.

parameters.name: fin_length
parameters.justification: Fin length in m typical of air-source evaporator fins; branched rete-like geometry keeps fin efficiency high.

parameters.name: fin_thickness
parameters.justification: Aluminium fin thickness in m, standard for finned-tube heat exchangers.

parameters.name: fin_spacing
parameters.justification: Fin pitch in m; narrow spacing mimics dense rete capillaries, bounded by frosting and pressure drop.

parameters.name: heat_transfer_coefficient
parameters.justification: W/(m^2 K) forced-air convection on evaporator fins.

parameters.name: temperature_difference
parameters.justification: K between ambient air and refrigerant-side fin base; this external heat source is what makes COP > 1 possible.
